recent_articles.title: Cabinet clears amendment to make insult to Vande Mataram a punishable offence - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Union Cabinet** approved amendments to the Prevention of Insults To National Honour Act, 1971, making any insult or obstruction to the singing of "Vande Mataram" a punishable offense.  This decision follows the BJP's victory in West Bengal and comes after the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) issued guidelines urging the use of all six stanzas of the song at official events. The 1971 Act currently punishes those who prevent or disrupt the singing of the Indian National Anthem, but this amendment would broaden its scope to include "Vande Mataram".

recent_articles.title: Any casteist exclusion cannot be part of religion, says Supreme Court - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** ruled that any practice excluding people based on caste is not religious in nature, citing Article 25 of the Constitution. Justice B.V. Nagarathna emphasized this during a hearing regarding a Parsi woman's (Goolrokh Gupta) case who was barred from entering a fire temple for marrying outside her faith.  The court heard arguments that such restrictions resemble an "excommunication" and violate fundamental rights, referencing the "Doctrine of Coverture" which holds women lose their identity upon marriage.
